title: Per-interaction utility credits — thought fragments
content:
Goal: sketch a very compact per-interaction "utility credit" model that maps naturally to our inference costs (tokens, latency SLO, caching) and is friendly for tiny/viral flows. Lightweight, easy to explain to PMs + design.

Context / constraints
- Users want simple mental models ("X credits per message") not raw tokens.
- We need anchors for: short chat, long chat, embedding call, multimodal prompt.
- Must expose levers for SLO-backed tiers (latency premium) and Dedicated/Private customers (commit discounts).
- Keep an eye on batching/caching effects — credits should decay with reuse.

High-level idea
- Define a base unit: 1 utility credit approximates the cost to serve ~100 tokens of generated+input work at baseline model/hosted profile.
- Map common actions to credit buckets: quick prompt (1–3 credits), long reply (3–12 credits), embedding (0.5–2 credits per vector) depending on dim/alg.
- Apply multipliers: latency premium (x1.5 for <100ms median), quality premium (x1.2 for larger models), cache hit discount (x0.2 for prefix KV hit), dedicated discount (x0.6).

Assumptions (ballpark numbers for calc clarity)
- average short interaction: 40 tokens in, 120 tokens out = 160 tokens total
- average long interaction: 120 in, 600 out = 720 tokens total
- embedding call (single vector): 0 tokens generation but model compute ~0.02 GPU-second equivalent (we map to tokens)
- infra blended baseline cost per 1M tokens served (hosted, amortized across models + infra): $2,500 (this includes GPU, infra, networking, monitoring). => $0.0025 per token
- developer-facing price target: want gross margin ~60% at scale on hosted public API

Back-of-envelope math
- Short interaction (160 tokens) infra cost = 160 * $0.0025 = $0.40
- Long interaction (720 tokens) infra cost = 720 * $0.0025 = $1.80

If 1 utility credit ≈ infra cost of 100 tokens => cost per credit = 100 * $0.0025 = $0.25 (unit cost)
We want to charge retail price = cost / (1 - margin) with margin 60% => price per credit = $0.25 / 0.4 = $0.625

Map interactions to credits
- Short interaction ~160 tokens => 1.6 credits -> round to 2 credits => price = 2 * $0.625 = $1.25 (list)
- Long interaction ~720 tokens => 7.2 credits -> round to 7 credits => price = 7 * $0.625 = $4.375 -> maybe price $4.25 (market friendliness)

Counters and observations
- Those per-interaction prices look plausible for paid endpoints but feel high for viral consumer flows. We can offset via:
  - free tier with small monthly credit grant (e.g., 50 credits/month)
  - micro-credits priced lower as a starter bundle (volume-based pricing)
  - amortize model selection by routing cheaper models for background/low-quality work

Caching and batching effects
- Cache hit: if we hit prefix/KV cache for generation, incremental tokens served drop dramatically. Give big discount: credit multiplier 0.2–0.3 for hits.
- Batching: increases infra efficiency (lower per-token GPU time) but doesn't change the external token accounting. Model: batching reduces effective cost per token by up to 30% at high concurrency; translate to lower internal cost per credit for committed seats.

Embedding mapping
- Map 1 vector to 0.5 credits at retail price => $0.3125
- For many-vector calls (n vectors): offer per-1000-vector discounts and a specialized bulk band.

Tier sketch (user-facing)
- Free: 50 credits / month (good for ~25 short interactions)
- Starter: 200 credits / month @ $19 (effective credit price = $0.095)
- Pro: 2,500 credits / month @ $199 (eff credit price = $0.0796)
- Scale: enterprise volume pricing + commit-based discounts (dedicated: credits cost x0.6)

Quick elasticity check
- If list credit price = $0.625 and Starter $19 for 200 credits => implied price per credit = $0.095 -> that's a 85% off list, which is fine as a bundle incentive. Need to ensure unit economics still work: with 60% gross margin target, heavy discounting on micro-bundles is subsidized by usage caps and conversion assumptions.
- Alternative: anchor by giving larger credits but expire (monthly) to prevent hoarding.

Edge cases & questions
- How to surface model quality differences? Option: attach a "quality footprint" multiplier to credits (small model = base, high quality model = x1.25). But must be simple.
- Long background generations (streaming + long context) can blow credits unexpectedly. Consider per-call caps (max credits billed per call) or require advanced notice for very long jobs.
- SLO premium should be electrically simple: a per-route multiplier. E.g., <100ms median route = x1.5.

Experiment ideas (A/B candidates)
- A: 1-credit baseline = 100 tokens, but show token-equivalents in UI for transparency.
- B: Use two currency units: "credits" for UI simplicity and show real token counts on billing page; measure conversion and confusion.
- C: Free starter group: 200 credits but restrict high-quality models until paid upgrade.

Next steps / TODOs
- Run micro-simulation (synthetic workload with token distribution) to validate average revenue per MAU for proposed bundles. Use existing usage histograms from /analytics or request Ben for sample exports.
- Draft V1 billing mapping doc for engineering: credit conversion table per model profile, caching multipliers, per-route premiums.
- Quick UX copy for how to explain credits in signup flow (2-sentence elevator + example interactions).

Loose notes (brain dump)
- Could anchor credit = 50 tokens instead of 100 to make price-per-credit feel smaller (psych effect). But more granular units create larger numbers in UI.
- For Dedicated customers, map credits to predictable GPU-hours rather than token heuristics and let them opt-in to token-count billing vs GPU-hour billing.
- Consider session-based subsidies (first N messages per session free / discounted) to drive stickiness.

Unresolved
- exact infra blended cost per token (need infra to confirm) — this number changes with quantization and model choice; use per-model profiles.
- embedding cost mapping needs validation against throughput benchmarks and vector dims.

Topline for a PM pitch
- One-line: "Introduce a small, standard 'utility credit' unit that maps to ~100 tokens of work, with simple multipliers for latency/quality/caching and easy starter bundles to make the product approachable for viral use while retaining predictable economics for scale."

End of notes.
